Bryn keeps the public records. The story takes place at the weaving shed. The reed basket must remain intact. No character may be physically injured. Keep practical actions precise. Use third-person past tense centred on Nell. Plan three chapters, each targeting 750 words. No earlier book or borrowed fictional world is assumed.

texts:
Nell received the sealed reed basket and checked its outer label. The weaving shed was open, though there were no visitors at the table. Nell cleared a space before setting anything down. Oli moved the loose tools to a tray and waited for instructions. Neither of them treated a late delivery as proof of a lost object. They checked what they could see and left a blank beside what they could not yet establish.

The work required a little patience. A faded number was difficult to distinguish from a stain, so Nell turned the sheet towards the window rather than writing over it. Oli read the number aloud. They compared their readings, found that they agreed, and entered it only once. The reed basket remained intact on the cleared table throughout the check.

Nell made a short note of the work completed that day. The note separated observation from intention: a task written for tomorrow did not become a task already done. Oli asked whether the uncertainty meant they should abandon the demonstration. Nell said that an unanswered question was a reason to check, rather than a reason to invent an answer. It was an ordinary distinction, but making it aloud helped them continue without blaming anyone.

Nell noticed a red seam but left it unopened. They put the tools back in the tray. Nell recorded that result and closed the current work period. The next planned task remained unwritten in the story. No one had opened a different room, visited another site, or completed the later demonstration in the interval between these actions.
